A methane reading edited before the audit. A cold-chain log smoothed over. Every offline field record has the same flaw: keep it private, and anyone can rewrite it.
Publish it, and you leak what's inside. Across three billion biodiversity records, Science warned that open sightings become a live map for poachers.
Vickrey starts with the seal. The phone only suggests a name. You decide, and that decision is signed on the device, and chained to the last entry.
Edit a copy waiting to sync, and the seal cracks. Sync refuses to send it. Put it back, and it verifies.

But proof still left a trail. So we moved the anchor into Zcash's shielded pool. Same transaction. Same amount. No name, no species, no place. Which one is yours? Only the verifier knows, and only if you hand over the receipt.
A stranger can ask one thing: does this transaction exist, at this height? There is no list to read. Nothing to enumerate.
This film's script is sealed the same way. Its hash, anchored. Check it.
Vickrey proved that a sealed bid makes people honest. We asked the same of a memory, without telling anyone where the bird was.
